phases.title: Before the move: fix the blockers and make the decisions
phases.intro: Everything here is settled while the account is still at its current position. NO-GO steps block the move; REVIEW steps need a decision or a check by hand.

steps.detail: Nothing says whether workloads.policies was inspected, so an empty list there cannot be told from one that was never read. It decides resource policies conditioned on the organization ID or path, which change meaning when the account moves. Collect the snapshot again with this version of orgshift once the cause is fixed, or add the entries by hand and record them under coverage.domains; for a hand-written snapshot, set coverage.asserted_complete once every list is confirmed. Until it is collected the verdict rests on incomplete evidence and a GO is not issued.

steps.title: Hand over delegated administration for config.amazonaws.com before the account leaves
steps.detail: If the account is a delegated administrator, the delegated administrator permissions have to be deregistered before it is migrated, whatever the procedure: a direct transfer, RemoveAccountFromOrganization and LeaveOrganization all fail until then (or until another account that stays is made the administrator). Deregister through the service's console or API, or with the Organizations deregister-delegated-administrator call where the service supports it. The service's organization-wide view, and often its member enrolment, moves with the role. Some services need the administrator disabled in the service itself first (GuardDuty, Security Hub, Macie, Inspector and Detective have a disable-organization-admin-account call); the organization-wide view of the service moves to the stand-in.
steps.finding: Account is the delegated administrator for config.amazonaws.com

steps.title: Lift the deny on organizations:LeaveOrganization in SCP Larkspur-Baseline-Guardrails / DenyLeaveOrganization for the transfer
steps.detail: Accepting the invitation needs organizations:LeaveOrganization, because accepting moves the account out of its organization, and in o-larkspur0001 it is denied by Larkspur-Baseline-Guardrails, DenyLeaveOrganization, attached at root Root (r-lark). An SCP in the source organization that denies it blocks the transfer even when the account's own IAM policy allows it. Lift the deny for the principal that accepts the invitation, for the duration of the transfer. Removal by the source management account is not part of a direct transfer: it is the leave-and-rejoin procedure, with a standalone interval and the standalone-account prerequisites.

steps.title: Plan the interval at the destination root: accept and move in one change
steps.detail: A migrated account is added to the root of the new organization; it reaches OU Core (ou-fern-core) only when the destination management account moves it there. Until then only the policies attached to the root apply. Not in force during that interval: SCP aws-guardrails-ztmvqe at OU Core (ou-fern-core). OU Core (ou-fern-core) is registered with Control Tower; at the root the account is not governed and cannot be enrolled. None of the actions in use or inbound requests in the usage list is decided differently at the root; the difference is in what the account could do, not in what the list says it does. Move the account in the same change as the acceptance, and treat anything done in between as done without the target OU's guardrails. The verdict board evaluates the target position; this finding is the root position. The move step that follows the acceptance in this runbook closes the interval; have the destination management account ready to run it as soon as the account has joined.
steps.finding: The account lands at the destination root first: 1 policy(ies) of the target path do not apply until it is moved into OU Core (ou-fern-core)

steps.title: Find what references the 2 AWSReservedSSO_* role(s) of the account
steps.detail: When the account leaves the organization, Identity Center cleans up the resources it created in the account; the documentation names the service-linked role, and the IAM roles provisioned for permission sets (path /aws-reserved/sso.amazonaws.com/us-east-1/) go with the instance's control over the account, so plan for them to disappear and confirm in IAM after the move. Anything that names these roles breaks: resource and trust policies, KMS key policies, S3 bucket policies, EKS access entries, pipelines and tools that assume them, and CloudTrail history keeps the old ARNs. The target instance provisions new roles with a different random suffix, so references have to be updated, not restored. The exact suffix is only visible in IAM; offline the roles are known by their pattern. List the exact role ARNs now, while they exist, and search for them so the references can be updated after the move.

phases.title: Before the move: re-create what does not travel
phases.intro: Shares, delegations, permission sets and stacks that are scoped to the account's current position do not follow it. Prepare the replacements now so nothing is interrupted.

steps.title: Re-share larkspur-core-network with the account directly: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule
steps.detail: Owner 111111111112 shares larkspur-core-network (ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule) with arn:aws:organizations::111111111111:organization/o-larkspur0001 today. After the move those principals no longer cover the account. Ask the owner to add account 111111111113 as a principal before the move so nothing attached to these resources is interrupted. The account will be outside the organization, so the share has to allow external principals and the account has to accept an invitation. The documentation says traffic or a declared operation stops with this share, so the move stays NO-GO until it is done: Shared by account 111111111112 with organization o-larkspur0001. It is scoped to the source organization or one of its OUs and stops applying when the account leaves. What the documentation says happens: ec2:Subnet: existing participant resources continue to run in the subnet; no new resources can be created in it, while existing ones can still be modified, described and deleted (subnets can only be shared inside one organization). ec2:Subnet can only be shared inside one organization, so it cannot be re-shared with the account once it has left. ec2:TransitGateway: existing transit gateway attachments remain functional; the account can no longer describe the transit gateway or create new attachments, and either side can delete the attachments. route53resolver:ResolverRule: traffic is affected at once, the rule's associations with the account's VPCs are removed and Resolver answers those queries from the remaining rules at once (an OU-scoped rule keeps its associations only when it is also shared with the destination OU). Ask the owner to re-share the resources with the account directly before the move, with external principals allowed, and accept the invitation after the move.
steps.finding: Networking share larkspur-core-network is lost: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule

phases.title: The move
phases.intro: A direct transfer: the destination invites, the account accepts, and that acceptance takes it out of its organization and into the destination's root in one step. It is never standalone. Run the move into the target OU straight after.

steps.title: Invite the account into Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001)
steps.detail: The invitation (a handshake) is valid for 15 days. Nothing changes for the account until it accepts.
commands: aws organizations invite-account-to-organization --target Id=111111111113,Type=ACCOUNT --notes "Move of larkspur-security planned with orgshift"

steps.title: Accept the invitation: the account changes organization
steps.detail: Accepting is the transfer: the account leaves Larkspur Holdings (o-larkspur0001) and joins Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001) at its root in the same step, with the AWS managed default policies attached. It does not run leave-organization and is never standalone, but the principal that accepts needs organizations:LeaveOrganization as well as organizations:AcceptHandshake, and no SCP of the source may deny it. From this moment no SCP, RCP or tag policy of the source applies, organization-scoped shares stop reaching the account and Identity Center deletes its roles in it.
commands: aws organizations accept-handshake --handshake-id <handshake ID from the previous command>

steps.title: Move the account from the root to OU Core (ou-fern-core)
steps.detail: Until this call the account sits at the target root with only the policies attached there.

phases.title: After the move: checks
phases.intro: Confirm what the simulation predicted and finish what could only be done once the account is at its new position.

steps.title: Delete the role that lets 111111111111 into the account, and give Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001) its own
steps.detail: The account was created in the source organization, which created an IAM role (OrganizationAccountAccessRole unless another name was given) that the source management account can assume. When an account leaves an organization, any IAM role that was created to give the organization's management account access is not deleted. To end that access from the former organization's management account, delete the role by hand; the destination management account needs a role of its own, since Organizations does not create one for an invited account. Look at the role's trust policy first: delete it only when it trusts the former management account and nothing else depends on it.

steps.title: Enroll the account in Control Tower from Account Factory (OU Core)
steps.detail: Moving into a registered OU applies the OU's SCPs at once (the 1 preventive guardrail SCP(s) on the chain are attached to the OUs), but the 1 detective control(s) do not report and the baseline is not deployed until the account is enrolled. Enrolment is done from Account Factory (enroll account) and needs an AWSControlTowerExecution role in the account that trusts management account 222222222221, no Config recorder or delivery channel of the account's own in the governed regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), and an email address and name that Account Factory can register. The account has to have joined o-fernhill0001 before it can be enrolled.
steps.where: management account 222222222221 of Fernhill Group (Account Factory)
steps.finding: Target OU Core is registered with Control Tower; the account has to be enrolled
commands: # Control Tower console → Account Factory → Enroll account → larkspur-security, OU OU Core (ou-fern-core)

evidence.note: version 3.3, status ACTIVE, drift IN_SYNC; home region eu-west-1; governed regions eu-west-1, eu-central-1; auto-enrollment disabled

steps.title: Update references to the deleted AWSReservedSSO_* roles with the ARNs the target instance provisions
steps.detail: The new roles have a different random suffix. Replace the old ARNs found before the move in resource policies, key policies, EKS access entries and tooling.
steps.finding: 2 AWSReservedSSO_* role(s) are deleted from the account: AWSReservedSSO_AdministratorAccess_*, AWSReservedSSO_ReadOnlyAccess_*

steps.title: Assign AdministratorAccess to group Platform-Admins for the account in the target instance
steps.detail: Users and groups in identity store d-fern0000001 are different objects from the source ones, so look each one up by name first; create it there if it is missing. Identity Center then provisions a new AWSReservedSSO_AdministratorAccess_* role in the account.
steps.where: Identity Center of Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001) (account 222222222221, eu-west-1)
steps.finding: Permission set AdministratorAccess: 1 assignment(s) removed when the account leaves (group Platform-Admins)
commands: aws sso-admin create-account-assignment --instance-arn arn:aws:sso:::instance/ssoins-fernhill00000001 --target-id 111111111113 --target-type AWS_ACCOUNT --permission-set-arn arn:aws:sso:::permissionSet/ssoins-fernhill00000001/ps-fern00000001 --principal-type GROUP --principal-id <ID from the previous command>

steps.title: Assign ReadOnlyAccess to group Security-Auditors for the account in the target instance
steps.detail: Users and groups in identity store d-fern0000001 are different objects from the source ones, so look each one up by name first; create it there if it is missing. Identity Center then provisions a new AWSReservedSSO_ReadOnlyAccess_* role in the account.
steps.where: Identity Center of Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001) (account 222222222221, eu-west-1)
steps.finding: Permission set ReadOnlyAccess: 1 assignment(s) removed when the account leaves (group Security-Auditors)
commands: aws sso-admin create-account-assignment --instance-arn arn:aws:sso:::instance/ssoins-fernhill00000001 --target-id 111111111113 --target-type AWS_ACCOUNT --permission-set-arn arn:aws:sso:::permissionSet/ssoins-fernhill00000001/ps-fern00000002 --principal-type GROUP --principal-id <ID from the previous command>

steps.title: Collect a fresh snapshot and simulate the account at its new position
steps.detail: With the account inside the target organization, a simulation of the account against its own parent compares it with itself and should come back GO, which closes the runbook.

phases.title: Rollback
phases.intro: If something breaks, this puts the account back where it was. Built from the source policy chain of the simulation.

steps.title: Have Larkspur Holdings (o-larkspur0001) invite the account back, and accept
steps.detail: The way back is another transfer: the source management account invites, the account accepts and comes back at the source root with the AWS managed defaults only. The same eligibility requirements apply in this direction, and the principal that accepts needs organizations:LeaveOrganization in the target. The target chain denies organizations:LeaveOrganization (Fernhill-Root-Guardrails / DenyLeaveOrganization at root Root (r-fern)): that blocks a direct transfer back, so lift it for the principal that accepts, or have the target management account remove the account, which makes it standalone first and needs the standalone-account information.
steps.where: management account 111111111111 of Larkspur Holdings, then account larkspur-security (111111111113)

steps.title: Move the account back to OU Security (ou-lark-sec)
steps.detail: Restores the original chain of OU attachments.

steps.title: Re-create the 2 Identity Center assignment(s) in the source instance
steps.detail: The source identity store still has the users and groups; the principal IDs below come from the snapshot. New AWSReservedSSO_* roles are provisioned with new suffixes, so references to the old ARNs do not come back by themselves.
steps.where: Identity Center of Larkspur Holdings (o-larkspur0001) (account 111111111111, us-east-1)
commands: aws sso-admin create-account-assignment --instance-arn arn:aws:sso:::instance/ssoins-larkspur00000001 --target-id 111111111113 --target-type AWS_ACCOUNT --permission-set-arn arn:aws:sso:::permissionSet/ssoins-larkspur00000001/ps-lark00000001 --principal-type GROUP --principal-id ba31fe89-32df-0f24-6b40-1c6f590a40ff   # group Platform-Admins

aws sso-admin create-account-assignment --instance-arn arn:aws:sso:::instance/ssoins-larkspur00000001 --target-id 111111111113 --target-type AWS_ACCOUNT --permission-set-arn arn:aws:sso:::permissionSet/ssoins-larkspur00000001/ps-lark00000003 --principal-type GROUP --principal-id fd2d8b09-2a71-ec4a-cc89-1ddb07a87174   # group Security-Auditors

steps.title: Re-delegate administration to the account: config.amazonaws.com, guardduty.amazonaws.com, securityhub.amazonaws.com
steps.detail: Only if the hand-over before the move is to be reversed; deregister the stand-in first.

steps.title: Organization-scoped shares and the organization trail cover the account again on their own
steps.detail: Shares offered to the source organization or its OUs, the organization trail, the Config aggregator and service-managed StackSets follow membership and need no action. Shares that owners narrowed to the account ID keep working as well.
